question: Which participle/verb form best fits? (1)
solution:
The correct answer is '**resulting**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The passage discusses the ongoing global health concern of low hemoglobin levels among women and its root causes.
 
• The appropriate word should connect the main clause to the causes without needing a new subject or conjunction.
 
• "**Resulting**" fits perfectly as a present participle. It acts as a reduced relative clause (meaning "which often results from"), smoothly linking the health condition to its causes.
 
• Other options ("**result**", "**results**", "**resulted**") do not fit grammatically because they are conjugated verbs that would require a conjunction or a relative pronoun to attach properly to the sentence.

Therefore, the correct answer is '**Option 1**'.

 

Complete Passage: *Low hemoglobin levels among women remain a pervasive global health concern, often 1. resulting__ from nutritional deficiencies, chronic diseases, or socio-economic disparities. In many developing nations, iron-deficiency anemia (2)_____. an alarming proportion of the female population, with consequences that extend beyond fatigue to impair cognitive performance and maternal outcomes. Medical experts emphasize that anemia is often (3) insidious, progressing stealthily until severe symptoms manifest. Despite the availability of supplements and fortified foods, adherence to preventive strategies (4) ______hampered by cultural taboos, misinformation, and healthcare. Furthermore, in many societies, menstruation and related issues are still shrouded in (5) obfuscation, limiting open dialogue and delaying early intervention. Addressing this silent epidemic requires not only medical solutions but also robust public health campaigns aimed at education and destigmatization. Bridging empowering women and fostering healthier generations. sing the gap between awareness and action is crucial to*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• Result (परिणाम/उत्पन्न होना): Base form of the verb or a noun. It does not fit the required participial phrase structure.
 
• Results (उत्पन्न होता है): Third-person singular present verb. It requires a singular subject or a relative pronoun (e.g., "which results").
 
• Resulted (उत्पन्न हुआ): Past tense verb. It is incorrect for a sentence stating a general, ongoing present fact.
